addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- trello-skill: Use when the user asks to create, manage, or query Trello boards, lists, cards, labels, members, checklists, or comments
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use App\Http\Controllers\UserController;
use App\Services\Api\AuthService;
use GuzzleHttp\Client;

/*
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------
| Web Routes
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------
|

| routes are loaded by the RouteServiceProvider within a group which
| contains the "web" middleware group. Now create something great!
|
*/

Route::get('/', function () {
    return view('welcome');
});

Route::get('/dashboard', function () {
    return view('dashboard');
})->middleware(['auth'])->name('dashboard');

require __DIR__.'/auth.php';


/**
 * inizia procedura di iscrizione webhook strava
 */
Route::get("/subscription", function(Client $connectedClient) {

    try {
        $connectedClient->post("push_subscriptions", [
            'form_params' => [
                'client_id' => config("strava.client_id"),
                'client_secret' => config("strava.client_secret"),
                'callback_url' => config('app.url').'/api/webhook',
                'verify_token' => config("strava.subscription_token"),
            ]
        ]);

    } catch (\GuzzleHttp\Exception\ClientException $e) {
        ddd($e->getResponse()->getBody()->getContents());
    }

});


/**
 * Oauth per app da utente
 */
Route::get("/authorize", [UserController::class, 'authorize'])->name("authorize");
Route::get("/authorize/callback",  [UserController::class, 'authorizeCallback'])->name("authorize.callback");

<?php

namespace App\Models;

use Carbon\Carbon;
use DateTimeInterface;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;

/**
 * A single activity by an user
 */
class Activity extends Model
{
    use SoftDeletes;

    /**
     * The table associated with the model.
     *
     * @var string
     */
    protected $table = 'activities';


    /**
     * The attributes that are OT mass assignable.
     *
     * @var array
     */
    protected $fillable = [
        "user_id",
        "ext_id",
        "ext_user_id",
        "name",
        "distance",
        "moving_time",
        "elapsed_time",
        "total_elevation_gain",
        "type",
        "sport_type",
        "start_date",
        "start_date_local",
        "end_date",
        "end_date_local",
        "timezone",
        "utc_offset",
        "manual",
        "flagged",
        "average_speed",
        "max_speed",
        "gear_id",
        "location_city",
        "location_state",
        "location_country",
        'calories',
        'raw_data',
    ];



    /**
     * The "booting" method of the model.
     *
     * @return void
     */
    protected static function boot()
    {
        parent::boot();

    }


    /**
     * Utente di appartenenza
     */
    public function user()
    {
        return $this->belongsTo("App\User");
    }


    /**
     * Valid
     */
    public function scopeValid($query)
    {

        // teoricamente la condizione su race_week non serve,
        // la inserisco per comodità nel fare i test
        // per poter impostare manualmente la colonna eligible a 1)
        return $query->where([['eligible', 1], ["race_week", '>', 0]]);
    }



    /**
     * settimana specifica
     */
    public function scopeForWeek($query, $week_number)
    {
        return $query->where('race_week', $week_number);
    }


    /**
     * Maps activity data into own attributes
     */
    public static function mapFromStrava(array $data): array
    {
        return [
            'ext_user_id' => $data['athlete']['id'],
            'name' => $data['name'],
            'distance' => $data['distance'],
            'moving_time' => $data['moving_time'],
            'elapsed_time' => $data['elapsed_time'],
            'total_elevation_gain' => $data['total_elevation_gain'],
            'type' => $data['type'],
            'sport_type' => $data['sport_type'],
            'start_date' => Carbon::parse($data['start_date']),
            'start_date_local' => Carbon::parse($data['start_date_local']),
            'end_date' => Carbon::parse($data['start_date'])->addSeconds($data['elapsed_time']),
            'end_date_local' => Carbon::parse($data['start_date_local'])->addSeconds($data['elapsed_time']),
            'timezone' => $data['timezone'],
            'gear_id' => $data['gear_id'],
            'calories' => $data['calories'],
            'average_speed' => $data['average_speed'],
            'max_speed' => $data['max_speed'],
            'description' => $data['description'],
            'location_city' => $data['location_city'],
            'location_state' => $data['location_state'],
            'location_country' => $data['location_country'],
            'calories' => $data['calories'],
            'raw_data' => json_encode($data),
        ];
    }


    /**
     * Get all activities that has started from a given date.
     */
    public function scopeFrom(Builder $query, DateTimeInterface $date)
    {
        return $query->where('start_date', '>=', $date);
    }

    /**
     * Get all activities that has ended before a given date.
     */
    public function scopeTo(Builder $query, DateTimeInterface $date)
    {
        return $query->where('end_date', '<=', $date);
    }

}

namespace App\Models;

use Exception;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\MustVerifyEmail;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User as Authenticatable;
use Illuminate\Notifications\Notifiable;
use League\OAuth2\Client\Token\AccessTokenInterface;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
use DateTime;
use App\Providers\RouteServiceProvider;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\HasMany;

class User extends Authenticatable
{
    use HasFactory;
    use Notifiable;
    use SoftDeletes;

    /**
     * The attributes that are mass assignable.
     *
     * @var array
     */
    protected $fillable = [
        'name',
        'email',
        'password',
        "user_id",
        "ext_id",
        "username",
        "resource_state",
        "firstname",
        "lastname",
        "city",
        "state",
        "country",
        "sex",
        "premium",
        "summit",
        "ext_created_at",
        "ext_updated_at",
        "badge_type_id",
        "profile_medium",
        "profile"
    ];

    /**
     * The attributes that should be hidden for arrays.
     *
     * @var array
     */
    protected $hidden = [
        'password',
        'remember_token',
    ];

    /**
     * The attributes that should be cast to native types.
     *
     * @var array
     */
    protected $casts = [
        'email_verified_at' => 'datetime',
    ];

    /**
     * The "booting" method of the model.
     * Aggiungo controllo su stato active
     *
     * @return void
     */
    protected static function boot()
    {
        parent::boot();

        // static::addGlobalScope('active', function (Builder $builder) {
        //     $builder->where('active', 1);
        // });
    }


    /**
     * Connette utente ad applicazione
     */
    public function registerApp(AccessTokenInterface $data)
    {

        // controllo id
        $userId = $this->id;
        if(!strlen($userId)) {
            throw new Exception("User not loaded, this should not happen!");
        }

        // recupero valori
        $values = $data->getValues();

        // controllo che lo stesso utente strava non sia già presente in database
        $checkExtUser =  self::where([["ext_id", $values["athlete"]["id"]], ["id", '<>', $userId] ])->get();
        if ($checkExtUser->count()) {

            Log::channel('database')->info("utente strava già registrato: ".$userId."-".$values["athlete"]["id"], [
                "values" => $values
                ,"user-agent" => !empty($_SERVER["HTTP_USER_AGENT"]) ? $_SERVER["HTTP_USER_AGENT"] : ''
                ,"request" => !empty($_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"]) ? $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"] : ''
            ]);

            abort("400", "This Strava account is already registered.");
        }

        // aggiorno
        $this->ext_id = $values["athlete"]["id"];
        $this->username = $values["athlete"]["username"];
        $this->resource_state = $values["athlete"]["resource_state"];
        $this->firstname = $values["athlete"]["firstname"];
        $this->lastname = $values["athlete"]["lastname"];
        $this->city = $values["athlete"]["city"];
        $this->state = $values["athlete"]["state"];
        $this->country = $values["athlete"]["country"];
        $this->sex = $values["athlete"]["sex"];
        // formato esempio 2014-02-05T22:31:47Z
        $this->ext_created_at = (new DateTime($values["athlete"]["created_at"]));
        $this->ext_updated_at = (new DateTime($values["athlete"]["updated_at"]));
        $this->badge_type_id = $values["athlete"]["badge_type_id"];
        $this->profile_medium = $values["athlete"]["profile_medium"];
        $this->profile = $values["athlete"]["profile"];

        $this->token_expires_at = DateTime::createFromFormat('U', $data->getExpires());
        $this->token_expires_at_timestamp = $data->getExpires();
        $this->refresh_token = $data->getRefreshToken();
        $this->access_token = $data->getToken();
        $this->token_type = $values["token_type"];

        $this->save();

        return $this;

    }


    /**
     * Varifica stato di connessione con app
     */
    public function isConnected()
    {
        return $this->ext_id !== null && strlen($this->access_token) > 0 && strlen($this->refresh_token) > 0;
    }


    /**
     * Link profilo Strava
     */
    public function getStravaProfileLinkAttribute()
    {
        if(strlen($this->ext_id) === 0) {
            return null;
        }
        return 'https://www.strava.com/athletes/' . $this->ext_id;
    }


    /**
     * User's activities
     */
    public function activities(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(Activity::class, 'user_id');
    }

}

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Exceptions\StravaConnectScopeException;
use App\Providers\RouteServiceProvider;
use App\Services\Api\AuthService;
use Exception;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\Access\AuthorizesRequests;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Bus\DispatchesJobs;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Validation\ValidatesRequests;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Routing\Controller as BaseController;

class UserController extends BaseController
{
    use AuthorizesRequests, DispatchesJobs, ValidatesRequests;


    public function __construct()
    {
        $this->middleware("auth");
    }


    /**
     * Reindirizza a oath per collegamento utente-app
     */
    public function authorize(Request $request, AuthService $authService)
    {
        // url di rientro dopo autorizzazione: edit del profilo utente
        $authUrl = $authService->authorizationUrl(route("authorize.callback"), $request->user()->id);
        
        return redirect()->to($authUrl);

    }


    /**
     * Rientro dopo autorizzazione strava
     */
    public function authorizeCallback(Request $request, AuthService $authService)
    {
        $user = $request->user();

        // negazione permessi
        if($request->error && $request->error == 'access_denied') {
            throw new StravaConnectScopeException();
        } 
        
        // validazione
        if (!strlen($request->code)) {
            abort(400);
        }

        // controllo id utente prima di uscita
        $userId = $user->id;
        $exitUserId = $request->get("state");
        if ($exitUserId != $userId) {
            throw new Exception("Discrepanza id utente nel rientro da strava");
        }


        // validazione permessi
        $avalScopes = $request->scope ? explode(",", $request->scope) : [];
        if (!in_array("read", $avalScopes) || !in_array("activity:read", $avalScopes) ) {
            throw new StravaConnectScopeException($user);
        }
    
        // scambio il codice per i dati utente
        $data = $authService->tokenExchange($request->code);

        // salvo utente
        $user->registerApp($data);

        return redirect(RouteServiceProvider::HOME);


    }


}

namespace App\Services\Api;

use Throwable;
use Carbon\Carbon;
use App\Models\User;
use Strava\API\OAuth;
use GuzzleHttp\Client;
use League\OAuth2\Client\Token\AccessTokenInterface;

/**
 * Wrapper around strava apis to process 
 * users' registration and authorization
 */
class AuthService
{

    /**
     * Http client
     */
    protected Client $connectedAdapter;


    /**
     * @param Client $clientId
     * @param string $clientSecret
     */
    public function __construct(Client $client) {
        $this->connectedAdapter = $client;
    }

    
    /**
     * Istanzia ouath
     * // TODO passare da fuori ed eliminare accesso a config strava
     */
    protected function oauth($params = []) {
    
        $options = array_merge([
            'clientId'     => config('strava.client_id'),
            'clientSecret' => config('strava.client_secret'),
        ], $params);

        return new OAuth($options);

    }



    /**
     * Crea url di autorizzazione
     * @param string url di redirect dopo autorizzazione
     * @param mixed $state parametro ulteriore ritornato nella query di stringa di rientro da strava
     */
    public function authorizationUrl($redirectUrl, $state = null) {

        $oauth = $this->oauth(['redirectUri'  => $redirectUrl]);

        $params = [
            'response_type'   => 'code',
            'approval_prompt' => 'auto',
            'scope'=> ['activity:read']
        ];
        if ($state !== null) {
            $params["state"] = $state;
        }
                    
        return $oauth->getAuthorizationUrl($params);

    }


    /**
     * Scambia codice ricevuto in ritorno da autorizzazione per un token d'accesso.
     * Il token ritornato è un istanza di League\OAuth2\Client\Token\AccessTokenInterface.
     * @see https://oauth2.thephpleague.com/
     */
    public function tokenExchange($code) : ? AccessTokenInterface {

        $oauth = $this->oauth();

        $data = $oauth->getAccessToken('authorization_code', [
            'code' => $code
        ]);

        return $data;
    
    }


    /**
     * Refresh del token
     * @param string $refresh_token token dedicato al refresh ottenuto nella prima autenticazione
     */
    public function tokenRefresh(string $refresh_token)  : ? AccessTokenInterface {

        $data = $this->oauth()->getAccessToken($grant = 'refresh_token', $params = [
            "refresh_token" => $refresh_token,
        ]);     

        return $data;
    }



    /**
     * Check if a token needs refresh.
     * If so, refresh it and store it for the user.
     */
    public function checkAndRefreshTokenForUser(User $user) : string
    {   

        // se il token non è scaduto, im fermo
        // controllo la scadenza con un range
        $tokenExpire = Carbon::parse($user->token_expires_at);
        $validityTreshold = 30; // voglio almeno 30 secondi di validità

        // ho validità inferiore a quella desiderata, è scaduto
        if ($tokenExpire < (new Carbon())->addSeconds($validityTreshold)) {
            $token = $this->tokenRefresh($user->refresh_token);

            $user->access_token = $token->getToken();
            $user->refresh_token = $token->getRefreshToken();
            $user->token_expires_at_timestamp = $token->getExpires();
            $user->token_expires_at = Carbon::parse($token->getExpires());
            $user->save();

            // return new access token
            return $user->access_token;
        }

        // token is still valid, we can return it
        return $user->access_token;
    }


    
}

<?php

namespace App\Services\Rest;

use Strava\API\Service\REST;
use Strava\API\Service\ServiceInterface;

/**
 * Extends vendor RESt to forward exceptions to the outside
 */
class StravaRest extends REST implements ServiceInterface
{
    /**
     * Get an API request response and handle possible exceptions.
     *
     * @param string $method
     * @param string $path
     * @param array $parameters
     *
     * @return array|mixed|string
     * @throws \GuzzleHttp\Exception\GuzzleException
     */
    protected function getResponse($method, $path, $parameters)
    {
        try {
            $response = $this->adapter->request($method, $path, $parameters);
            $result = $this->getResult($response);

            if ($this->responseVerbosity === 0 && !is_string($result)) {
                return $result["body"];
            }

            return $result;
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            throw $e;
        }
    }
}

namespace App\Console\Commands;

use Carbon\Carbon;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Domain\StatsCalculator;
use Illuminate\Console\Command;
use App\Domain\Activity\ActivityTypeEnum;
use Exception;

class ActivitiesStats extends Command
{
    /**
     * The name and signature of the console command.
     *
     * @var string
     */
    protected $signature = 'activities:stats
        {--users= : comma separated ids of users}
        {--start= : start date (format Y-m-d)}
        {--end= : end date (format Y-m-d)}
        {--type= : activity type, must be a valid activity type enum key}
        {--gear= : id of gear}
    ';

    /**
     * The console command description.
     *
     * @var string
     */
    protected $description = 'Executes stats on activities';

    /**
     * Execute the console command.
     */
    public function handle()
    {
        $type = (string)strtoupper($this->option('type'));

        $service = new StatsCalculator();

        /**
         * Loop through options and call appropiate method on calculator
         */
        if($type) {
            $service->setActivityType(constant(ActivityTypeEnum::class . "::$type"));
        }

        if($this->option('start')) {
            $service->setStartDate(Carbon::parse($this->option('start')));
        }

        if($this->option('end')) {
            $service->setEndDate(Carbon::parse($this->option('end')));
        }

        if($this->option('users')) {
            $ids = explode(',', $this->option('users'));
            $users = User::whereIn('id', $ids)->get();
            if(count($users) < count($ids)) {
                throw new Exception("Some users were not found");
            }
            $service->setUsers($users);
        }

        if($this->option('gear')) {
            $service->setGearId((int)($this->option('gear')));
        }

    }
}

     * @var string
     */
    protected $description = 'Processes received webhooks';

    /**
     * Create a new command instance.
     *
     * @return void
     */
    public function __construct()
    {
        parent::__construct();
    }

    /**
     * Execute the console command.
     *
     * @return int
     */
    public function handle()
    {

        /**
         * Get unprocessed webhooks.
         * Set a limit of webhooks that will be processed.
         * Update limit value according to how many times the command will be
         * scheduled (s. Console\Kernel) and how jobs are rate limited.
         */
        $result = Webhook::where('processed', 'N')->orderBy('id')->limit(100)->get();


        /**
         * Dispatch a job for each webhook
         */
        foreach($result as $item) {
            WebhookProcess::dispatch($item);
        }

        return 0;
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Jobs;

use Strava\API\Client;
use App\Models\Webhook;
use App\Models\Activity;
use Illuminate\Bus\Queueable;
use App\Services\Api\AuthService;
use App\Services\Rest\StravaRest;
use GuzzleHttp\Client as Adapter;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Queue\SerializesModels;
use Illuminate\Queue\InteractsWithQueue;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Bus\Dispatchable;
use Illuminate\Queue\Middleware\RateLimited;

/**
 * Process a single webhook notification
 */
class WebhookProcess implements ShouldQueue
{
    use Dispatchable;
    use InteractsWithQueue;
    use Queueable;
    use SerializesModels;

    /**
     * @var Webhook the webhook being processed
     */
    protected $item;


    /**
     * The number of times the job may be attempted.
     *
     * @var int
     */
    public $tries = 20;

    /**
     * The maximum number of unhandled exceptions to allow before failing.
     *
     * @var int
     */
    public $maxExceptions = 3;

    /**
     * Create a new job instance.
     *
     * @return void
     */
    public function __construct(Webhook $item)
    {
        $this->item = $item;
    }

    /**
     * Execute the job.
     *
     *
     * @return void
     */
    public function handle(Adapter $adapter, AuthService $authService)
    {


        /**
         * If we are processing a "delete" aspect_type, try to locale the local activity
         * and delete it.
         */
        if($this->item->aspect_type == 'delete') {
            $activity = Activity::where('ext_id', $this->item->object_id)->first();
            if($activity) {
                $activity->delete();
            }
            $this->item->processed = 'Y';
            $this->item->save();
            return;
        }


        /**
         * get the owner
         */
        $user = $this->item->owner;
        if(!$user) {
            $this->item->status_code = 'user_not_found';
            $this->item->processed = 'Y';
            $this->item->save();
            return;
        }


        /**
         * Refresh token if needed
         */
        $token = $authService->checkAndRefreshTokenForUser($user);


        /**
         * Instantiate the client
         */
        $service = new StravaRest($token, $adapter);
        $apiClient = new Client($service);


        /**
         * Get the activity.
         * If activity is not found, it could be deleted on remote.
         */
        try {
            $activityData = $apiClient->getActivity($this->item->object_id);
        } catch (\GuzzleHttp\Exception\ClientException $e) {
            $statusCode = $e->getResponse()->getStatusCode();
            $this->item->status_code = $statusCode;
            $this->item->processed = 'Y';
            $this->item->save();
            if($statusCode == 404) {
                return;
            }
        }


        /**
         * Save the activity.
         * We do not care about aspect_type (create vs update),
         * we are going to save the last updated version.
         */
        Activity::updateOrCreate([
            'ext_id' => $activityData['id'],
        ], array_merge(
            [
                'user_id' => $user->id,
            ],
            Activity::mapFromStrava($activityData)
        ));

        /**
         * Update webhook
         */
        $this->item->processed = 'Y';
        $this->item->save();

    }

    /**
     * Get the middleware the job should pass through.
     *
     * @return array<int, object>
     */
    public function middleware(): array
    {
        return [new RateLimited('webhook_process')];
    }
}

Sì, ho esplorato la struttura e la comprendo. È un'applicazione **Laravel** che fa da log/tracker personale delle attività Strava, con questa architettura:

**Autenticazione e integrazione Strava**
- Login classico Laravel (Breeze/Fortify-style, in `routes/auth.php`) più un collegamento OAuth separato verso Strava (`UserController::authorize` / `authorizeCallback`), gestito da `AuthService` (usa `league/oauth2-client` tramite il wrapper `Strava\API\OAuth`).
- `User` model salva token Strava (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, `token_expires_at`) e dati atleta (nome, città, sesso, ecc.), con `registerApp()` che li popola dal callback OAuth e blocca se l'account Strava è già collegato a un altro utente.
- `AuthService::checkAndRefreshTokenForUser()` fa il refresh automatico del token se sta per scadere.

**Ricezione attività via webhook**
- Strava manda notifiche push a `WebhookController::webhook` (route `/api/webhook`), salvate grezze nella tabella `webhooks`.
- Il comando schedulato `webhooks:process` (`WebhooksProcess`) pesca i webhook non processati e lancia un job `WebhookProcess` per ciascuno (rate-limited).
- Il job recupera l'attività vera dalle API Strava (`StravaRest`, che estende la libreria `studio-42/elasticpress`... in realtà è un wrapper della libreria `strava-php` per propagare le eccezioni), gestisce `delete` come aspect_type, e fa `updateOrCreate` sul model `Activity` mappando i campi con `Activity::mapFromStrava()`.

**Dati e statistiche**
- `Activity` model ha scope utili (`valid`, `forWeek`, `from`, `to`) pensati per gare/settimane di gara (`race_week`, `eligible`).
- `StatsCalculator` (in `app/Domain`) è un builder di configurazione per calcolare statistiche (utenti, intervallo date, tipo attività via `ActivityTypeEnum`, gear) — al momento è **solo lo scaffolding**: i setter ci sono ma non c'è ancora nessun metodo che calcola/esegue le statistiche.
- Il comando `activities:stats` istanzia `StatsCalculator`, applica le opzioni da CLI, ma non chiama ancora nessun metodo di calcolo finale (coerente con lo stato "in progress" visto nell'ultimo commit "Stats calculation, begin").

In sintesi: l'app riceve webhook da Strava, sincronizza le attività dell'utente in un DB locale, e sta costruendo un motore di statistiche su queste attività (per gare/settimane), ma quella parte è ancora incompleta. Fammi sapere se vuoi che approfondisca una parte specifica (es. il modello dati delle attività, la logica di stats da implementare, o i test esistenti).

#
# 'docker-compose up'
#

version: "3"

services:
  web:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_web
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker-php.dockerfile
      args:
        # lasciare "#"
        - APACHE_RUN_USER=${COMPOSE_APACHE_RUN_USER}
        - APACHE_RUN_GROUP=${COMPOSE_APACHE_RUN_GROUP}
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh","-c"]
    command: 
      - |
        composer install
        php artisan migrate
        apache2-foreground
    restart: "no"
    volumes:
      - ".:/var/www/html"
      - "./docker-data/log:/var/log/apache2"
      - "./docker-data/php/php.ini:/usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/custom.ini"
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_WEB_PORT}

      # imposta l'hostname (come ritornato da gethostname()) INTERNAMENTE AL CONTAINER. Non ha effetto all'esterno
    hostname: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}.localhost
    # utente default di esecuzione dei comandi nel container, utilizza utente del sistema host (es. bash)
    user : ${COMPOSE_APACHE_RUN_USER}
    environment:
      - VIRTUAL_HOST=${COMPOSE_VIRTUAL_HOST:-}
    networks:
      - default
      - _external_
  db:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_db
    image: mysql:5.7
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: secret
      MYSQL_DATABASE : ${DB_DATABASE}
      MYSQL_USER : ${DB_USERNAME}
      MYSQL_PASSWORD : ${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./docker-data/mysql:/var/lib/mysql
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_MYSQL_PORT} 
    networks:
      - default
  # raggiungibile su {hostname}:5000
  phpmyadmin:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_pma
    image: phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin:5
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      PMA_HOST: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_db
      PMA_USER: root
      PMA_PASSWORD: secret
      UPLOAD_LIMIT : 200000000
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_PHPMYADMIN_PORT}
  node:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_node
    image : node:12
    command: >
      sh -c "npm install --save-dev && npm run watch"
    volumes:
      - "./:/app"
    working_dir: /app
    ports:
      - ${MIX_BROWSERSYNC_PORT}:${MIX_BROWSERSYNC_PORT}
networks:
  _external_:
    name : ${COMPOSE_EXTERNAL_NETWORK}
    external: true

content.content:
Configures the site and runs a series of standard project setup steps with
an interactive step-selector so you can toggle which steps to execute.

Before the step selector, lerd setup runs the lerd init wizard so you can
choose the PHP version, HTTPS, and required services. The answers are saved
to .lerd.yaml (commit it for portability). On subsequent runs, or when
.lerd.yaml already exists, the config is applied silently with no prompts.

Steps for all frameworks:
  1. composer install        — skipped if vendor/ already exists
  2. npm install/ci          — skipped if node_modules/ already exists (uses ci if lockfile exists)
  3. lerd env                — configure env file with lerd service settings
  4. lerd mcp:inject         — inject MCP config (off by default)
  5. npm run <build|production|prod> — build front-end assets (detected from package.json scripts)
  6. lerd secure             — enable HTTPS via mkcert (off by default)

Additional steps for Laravel projects:
  7. php artisan storage:link — create storage symlink
  8. php artisan migrate     — run database migrations
  9. php artisan db:seed     — seed the database (off by default)
  10. queue:start            — start queue worker
  11. stripe:listen          — start Stripe webhook listener (off by default)
  12. schedule:start         — start task scheduler
  13. reverb:start           — start Reverb WebSocket server (if configured)

Use --all to skip all selectors and run everything (useful in CI). In --all
mode with no .lerd.yaml, site registration falls back to auto-detection.

Usage:
  lerd setup [flags]

Flags:
  -a, --all         Select all steps without prompting (for CI/automation)
  -h, --help        help for setup
      --skip-open   Do not open the site in the browser at the end
=== check ===
Validate .lerd.yaml — PHP version, services, workers, container config, custom_workers, and db

Usage:
  lerd check [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for check
=== db:create ===
Create a database (and testing database) for the current project

Usage:
  lerd db:create [name] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for db:create
  -s, --service string   Lerd DB service to target (e.g. mysql, postgres)

<?php

use Laravel\Telescope\Http\Middleware\Authorize;
use Laravel\Telescope\Watchers;

return [

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Telescope Domain
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This is the subdomain where Telescope will be accessible from. If the
    | setting is null, Telescope will reside under the same domain as the
    | application. Otherwise, this value will be used as the subdomain.
    |
    */

    'domain' => env('TELESCOPE_DOMAIN', null),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Telescope Path
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This is the URI path where Telescope will be accessible from. Feel free
    | to change this path to anything you like. Note that the URI will not
    | affect the paths of its internal API that aren't exposed to users.
    |
    */

    'path' => env('TELESCOPE_PATH', 'telescope'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Telescope Storage Driver
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This configuration options determines the storage driver that will
    | be used to store Telescope's data. In addition, you may set any
    | custom options as needed by the particular driver you choose.
    |
    */

    'driver' => env('TELESCOPE_DRIVER', 'database'),

    'storage' => [
        'database' => [
            'connection' => env('DB_CONNECTION', 'mysql'),
            'chunk' => 1000,
        ],
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Telescope Master Switch
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This option may be used to disable all Telescope watchers regardless
    | of their individual configuration, which simply provides a single
    | and convenient way to enable or disable Telescope data storage.
    |
    */

    'enabled' => env('TELESCOPE_ENABLED', true),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Telescope Route Middleware
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | These middleware will be assigned to every Telescope route, giving you
    | the chance to add your own middleware to this list or change any of
    | the existing middleware. Or, you can simply stick with this list.
    |
    */

    'middleware' => [
        'web',
        Authorize::class,
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Allowed / Ignored Paths & Commands
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | The following array lists the URI paths and Artisan commands that will
    | not be watched by Telescope. In addition to this list, some Laravel
    | commands, like migrations and queue commands, are always ignored.
    |
    */

    'only_paths' => [
        // 'api/*'
    ],

    'ignore_paths' => [
        'nova-api*',
    ],

content.text: Lerd (DNS, PHP-FPM 8.4/8.5, watcher) è ora avviato correttamente. L'unico blocco è che **lerd-nginx non riesce a partire** perché la porta host 80 è già occupata dal container `traefik-reverse-proxy-1`, il reverse proxy che usi per gli altri progetti Docker Compose attivi (atmosphera-admin, atmosphera-hub, italamp). Lerd non espone un'opzione per usare porte diverse per il suo nginx (funziona come Herd/Valet: vuole 80/443 sull'host).

questions.question: Come vuoi risolvere il conflitto sulla porta 80 tra il nginx di lerd e Traefik (che serve gli altri tuoi progetti Docker attivi)?

options.label: Ferma Traefik temporaneamente (Recommended)
options.description: Eseguo 'docker stop traefik-reverse-proxy-1'. Gli altri siti (atmosphera-admin/hub, italamp) smetteranno di rispondere sui loro domini .localhost finché non riavvii Traefik tu stesso.

options.label: Lascia stare, accedo via IP/porta
options.description: Non tocco Traefik. Configuro comunque il sito in lerd (link + env + db) ma senza avviare lerd-nginx; userà direttamente php artisan serve per testare in locale.

options.label: Fermati, decido dopo
options.description: Non fare nulla sulla porta 80 per ora, continua solo con le parti che non richiedono nginx (env, database, migrazioni).

content.text:
Semplice: usi `lerd composer <argomenti>` da dentro la cartella del progetto (o con il sito già collegato), ed esegue quel comando composer dentro il container PHP del sito, con la versione PHP giusta e la cache condivisa di lerd.

Esempi:
```
lerd composer install
lerd composer require nome/pacchetto
lerd composer update
lerd composer dump-autoload
```

È l'analogo di `lerd console`/`lerd artisan` ma per composer invece che per il framework — non serve entrare nel container a mano.
